instructions:
The principal wants a yes/no answer. Using ONLY the listed fields (refer to each as
latest("<ref>")), write a decision rule as a boolean expression with explicit thresholds, the conventional or
physical reason for each threshold, and short labels for yes and no. The rationale must hold on any day: do not
mention today's values in it. If an existing service already gives a
direct verdict or index, you may use it, but prefer rules that remain correct if one source is missing (use 'or' /
'and' deliberately). A field that holds several numbers (e.g. hourly values "30 20 10 0") can be given to max(),
min() or sum(), e.g. max(latest("src:field")) >= 50. Allowed functions: latest, max, min, sum, round, coalesce,
if_else, max_over, min_over. Do not invent fields. One or two rules at most.

questions.quantity: Verdict (yes/no) on whether today's daytime weather in Osaka favors outdoor line-drying: no rain or precipitation expected during drying hours, plus supportive conditions (low humidity, some wind/sun, comfortable temperature). Verdict is based on forecast for today's daylight drying hours.
questions.question: Is today a good day to dry laundry outside in Osaka?
questions.population: Today's forecast for Osaka city, during daytime drying hours (roughly 08:00-18:00 local)

rules.question: Is today a good day to dry laundry outside in Osaka?
rules.expr: (sum(latest("met_2_0_compact:properties.timeseries.0.data.next_6_hours.details.precipitation_amount")) < 0.5) and (max(latest("tenki_27100_3hours_html:rain_probability_today")) < 40 or latest("tenki_27100_3hours_html:laundry_index_today") == "大変よく乾く") and (latest("met_2_0_compact:properties.timeseries.0.data.instant.details.relative_humidity") < 70) and (latest("met_2_0_compact:properties.timeseries.0.data.instant.details.air_temperature") >= 12)
rules.no_label: No – risk of rain or poor drying
rules.rationale: Laundry needs to stay dry first, so near-zero forecast precipitation is required from the met.no forecast, and tenki.jp rain probability must stay below about 40% (or tenki.jp rates drying as very good). Drying also needs air that can absorb moisture: relative humidity below about 70% is the usual line, since above it drying slows sharply. Temperature of at least about 12°C keeps evaporation reasonably fast. The rain test uses a short precipitation total plus the probability field so a single missing source does not decide the answer alone.

thresholds.why: Under half a millimetre is effectively dry; more would wet the laundry.
Below 40% chance of rain is a conventional low-risk cutoff for leaving washing out.
The tenki.jp top-rated index is a direct verdict that drying will be very good.
Evaporation slows markedly above about 70% relative humidity.
Below about 12°C evaporation is too slow for clothes to dry in a day.
